title: TypeScript SDK: runtime union resolvers and codegen ergonomics for streaming structured output
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Goal: make it straightforward for TypeScript users to (1) author discriminated union output contracts, (2) get robust runtime validators generated alongside type definitions, and (3) have a smooth streaming consumption experience that preserves structured output without brittle partial-parses. This ticket covers the runtime union resolver, a small codegen plugin to emit Zod + JSON Schema glue, and a set of examples demonstrating streaming-friendly decoder patterns and migration guidance for existing tSDK users.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Codegen emits stable .d.ts + corresponding Zod validators for union types that use a configurable discriminator field. 2) Runtime resolver chooses the correct zod validator for streaming partial-chunks and for progressive parse (token-by-token) without throwing on valid-but-incomplete content; it should surface a recoverable "NeedMoreData" signal. 3) Examples (chat, generation, reranker) exist in tsdk/examples/structured-output with README and tests. 4) Benchmarks show <5% latency regression for non-structured calls when validators are enabled. 5) Backcompat shim documented and enabled via opt-in flag.
implementation_notes:
- Introduce a small runtime abstraction: UnionResolver<T> that maps discriminator value -> validator. Keep the runtime minimal and tree-shakable.
- Codegen plugin emits: (a) types (.d.ts), (b) zod schemas, (c) a lightweight registry file that the runtime imports to wire type -> schema.
- Streaming: add a streaming parser helper (progressiveParse) that accumulates tokens and attempts incremental parse via zod.safeParse at checkpoints; on failure, return NeedMoreData rather than throwing.
- Provide an opt-in flag `structuredOutput: { enabled: true, discriminator: 'type' }` in the client call options. Default remains off for perf.
- Tests: unit test union resolution, integration test with /generate streaming responses, and a small perf harness to assert <5% overhead.
- Migration: publish a codemod in tsdk/migrations to add validator imports for common generators.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: validators could be expensive on hot request paths. Mitigation: make validators optional, support caching of last-used validator instance per route, and prefer schema shape checks that are shallow when using streaming checkpoints. Risk: discriminator collisions across model variants. Mitigation: add model-scoped registry and fallback policy; warn in console and in CI if collisions detected.
test_plan: 1) Unit: simulate partial and full payloads for union types and assert NeedMoreData vs success. 2) Integration: E2E with streaming API in a staging runtime using openai-compat model to emit structured JSON. 3) Perf: run 100k short calls (non-structured) with and without runtime enabled; record p50/p95. 4) QA: run manual smoke with example chat app and structured embed-to-action flow.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag `tsdk.structuredOutputV2`. 2) Dogfood within integrations team for 2 weeks. 3) Flip opt-in examples to use feature flag. 4) If metrics look good, enable opt-out for all new projects and document in changelog.
migration_notes: Existing users who relied on ad-hoc JSON parsing can switch by: 1) adding `structuredOutput: { enabled: true, discriminator: 'kind' }` to client init, 2) importing generated validators `import { MyUnionSchema } from './gen/schemas'`, or 3) running the codemod to insert schema imports into example output handlers.
